feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Evidence: iteration 2 (five sensors at ±0.04 m, wheel_track 0.10 m, mass 0.6 kg, kp 3.6, kd 0.6) scored 321, with oval finish rate 0.45 and s-bend finish rate 0.10 with max_error about 0.063 m. Iteration 1 (seven sensors at ±0.06 m) cut s-bend line loss from 1.1 to 0.2 but dropped the score to 86, so sensing is not the limit. What I compensated for in the controller: narrowing the track raises yaw per unit of PWM difference by about 1.11x, so I scaled kp from 3.6 to 3.3 to keep the steering gain steady, and kept kd at 0.6 to hold oscillation (0.27 oval, 0.43 s-bend in iteration 2). I cannot yet say whether this will hold the line on the s-bend. Please read the next race as follows. If max_error on the s-bend falls below 0.06 m and s-bend finish rate rises above 0.10, keep wheel_track narrowing as the main lever. If max_error stays near 0.063 m and line_loss_events stays near 0.9 with no completion gain, turn authority is no longer the limit, so change the sensor row before geometry again. If steering_oscillation rises well above 0.43 without line loss, the yaw gain is too high for this row, so move the sensors forward.
requested_changes: If s-bend line_loss_events stays near 0.9 and max_error still clusters at about 0.063 m, widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.05 m with the same five sensors and y = 0.04 m. Evidence: iteration 0 lost the tape at about ±0.058 m, and iteration 1 cut s-bend line loss from 1.1 to 0.2 when coverage was widened.

If steering_oscillation rises above the iteration 2 level (oval 0.27, s-bend 0.43) with no drop in line loss, move the sensor row forward to y = 0.06 m, keeping five sensors at ±0.04 m with 0.02 m spacing. Evidence: iteration 0 showed oscillation of 0.30 on the oval, and a higher effective yaw gain (from the narrower track) raises jitter at the same lookahead.

If the oval finish rate falls below 0.45 or completion_time worsens compared with iteration 2, return wheel_track to 0.10 m and keep mass at 0.6 kg with the same five-sensor row, because the narrower track has overshot. Evidence: iteration 2 (wheel_track 0.10, mass 0.6) reached 0.45 oval finish rate, and iteration 0 (wheel_track 0.12, mass 0.8) reached only 0.05.
